notes.text: The whole page was inspected once for layout and both native overlapping halves once line by line, including agreed words, formulas, deletions and insertions. All 21 unique enhanced crops were loaded successfully and inspected. No OCR, web research or TeX compilation was used.

The reader initially mistook the first short word for fully written composantes. Root identified the separate abbreviation stop. Reopening the same components_start crop established compos.; the candidate and evidence record preserve the abbreviation. The later canceled occurrence retains tentative composantes because its ending is not fully certified in the saved overlap. The final live occurrence is fully written composantes.

The equality with Sigma and the boundary-component definition are interlinear insertions. The long lower strokes accompanying cercles de raccord function as an insertion leader, so no independent underline is assigned. Old marquage is underlined and canceled; rigidification is above it. The period following the canceled trous phrase remains outside the cancellation.
The small crossed blob before the larger canceled S is physically indistinct. A literal stroke trace preserves it without assigning an underletter.

The first connector has a left hook, a long shaft and no right arrowhead. The trace reproduces this observed course. The second connector has a clear right arrowhead. No stronger arrow convention is imposed on the first connector.

Reader and root independently observed a substantial X-like form after the tall-stemmed oval. The candidate favors current partial X and retains an empty-set-plus-canceled-X alternative because the cancellation scope is not secure. A lone empty-set transcription would omit visible ink.

notes.place: finite-subset definition and second subgroupoid condition
notes.text: The definition visibly gives R included in Sigma. Only if the disputed second-row value is read as the empty set does ordinary inclusion force R to be empty. The current first reading is partial X, so this does not establish a contradiction in the source. The check event states the exact conditional argument.
The source defines arrows as isotopy classes of orientation-preserving homeomorphisms. This definition was transcribed; no additional mathematical verification was performed.
The source displays the variant with a sign map and names several full subgroupoids. Their fullness and the structural properties of the sign map were not independently proved in this reading.
The written tilde over the rightward arrow asserts an isomorphism between the two pi-zero expressions. The formula was read sign by sign, but its isomorphism claim was not checked.

The author writes that this case is not interesting, apparently except when Sigma also has the disputed empty-set value. This is preserved as the author’s assessment and is not treated as a proved mathematical claim.

Teich- and müller occupy successive lines. The inserted ou rigidifiés is enclosed by a continuous lower frame with curved side strokes. Only one closing parenthesis is visible after topologiques orientés; the transcription leaves the earlier outer opening unbalanced.
The top 2 belongs to the principal manuscript hand. The thinner gray lower-left 45 belongs to another unnamed hand and is kept as a margin item. No calendar date appears on the page.
The saved sigma_condition crop clips the very upper tip of the second tilde. The full tilde had already been read on the native half, and no second crop was made.
The larger canceled S forms, close, the old subscript and the thick empty-like values retain local doubts. Retracing alone has not been used to invent any earlier letter or digit.
